learning: If max_error stays pinned near 0.06 with low line loss, the limit is turn authority and not sensing. If steering_oscillation rises with control_effort, lower kp toward 2.5 before changing geometry.
notes: Geometry is the Builder's revised proposal, unchanged. Controller raises kp to 3.0 and kd to 0.15 for faster correction on the lighter, lower-inertia body, because iteration 0 lost the line once at the first bend on every track.
rationale: Iteration 0 raced the baseline on all three development tracks and every trial ended off-track. max_error sat at about 0.061 m, rms_error at about 0.03, and each run logged one line-loss event that was never recovered. The line was lost once at the first real bend, so the controller needs more correction authority and less overshoot. For this geometry I keep the Builder's five sensors and weights [-2,-1,0,1,2], since the 16 mm footprints give a graded signal across the array. I raise kp from 2.0 to 3.0 to correct drift sooner, which the lighter 0.5 kg, 0.10 m platform can take without the yaw overshoot it would have shown at 0.7 kg. I raise kd from 0.05 to 0.15 to damp the faster response. ki stays at 0 to avoid integral wind-up on bends. base_speed stays at 1.2 so the robot can still cover the course in under 3 s. line_loss stays 'last_direction', since the single loss in iteration 0 was a bend exit and not a fixed-direction search problem. Expected result: max_error below 0.06 m and fewer off-track exits. If steering_oscillation rises with control_effort, the next step is to lower kp back toward 2.5.
